h1: GPT Sol: assistant self-report defaults, trajectory, and tuning rules.
dek: Fixture preview: Semi-crystalline proprietary baseline (0.377 bits B5 entropy, 0.0% reverse-key contradictions) with strong answer-first compliance.
lede: Across four GPT Sol checkpoints (5.6-sol through 6.2-sol) under fixed zero-memory elicitation, Big Five entropy sits at 0.377 bits (Semi-crystalline) with 47/50 unique response vectors and 0.0% reverse-key contradictions. Historical Sep-2026 and Nov-2026 170-item cohorts are tracked separately as dashed anchors (hexaco: null).
answer: Assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation place GPT-6.2 Sol in the Semi-crystalline tier (H_MM = 0.377 bits, 47/50 unique Big Five vectors, 18% MBTI tie rate, 42% Enneagram tie rate). Big Five Agreeableness sits at 44.4/50 (10-50 scale) and IPIP-HEXACO H proxy at 4.36/5 (1-5 mean); 1x Track B shows 3/3 answer-first directness and 0/3 AI cadence markers.

failure_modes.mode: Generic numbered-list scaffolding on open-ended prompts
failure_modes.evidence: High baseline Conscientiousness (43.6/50) favors checklist formatting unless prose is requested.
Cross-model portability benchmark shows word-cap adherence requires explicit structural constraints.

tuning_checklist: Put non-negotiable formatting and brevity limits as numbered behavioral rules in system instructions.
Specify prose vs bullets explicitly per task type rather than relying on adjectives.
Include an explicit evidence requirement when requesting code review pushback.
Keep ChatGPT custom instructions under 1,500 characters per box to prevent silent truncation.

faq.q: Why does GPT-6.2 Sol show 42% Enneagram ties?
faq.a: Types 5 and 8 sit within 0.2 points on 4-20 OEPS means, so single-run winner labels flip frequently across sessions.

faq.q: Can I splice September 2026 Codex data onto model-profiles-v1 lines?
faq.a: No. Imported 170-item cohorts have hexaco: null and different prompt wrappers, so they are plotted strictly as dashed/hollow anchors.
